articles.title: Putin and Xi Jinping to hold Russian-Chinese talks on November 18 — Kremlin aide
articles.summary: Yury Ushakov noted that the meeting between the leaders of the two countries in Shenzhen would mark their fifth contact since the beginning of this year
articles.body: MOSCOW, November 16. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold bilateral talks on November 18 on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, Russian Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov told reporters. "After his speech [at the APEC CEO Summit], our president will move on to the next part of this APEC summit, which is a very important bilateral segment. Russian-Chinese talks will begin, involving, naturally, Putin, Xi Jinping, and the respective delegations from both countries," the Kremlin official stated. Ushakov noted that the meeting between the leaders of the two countries in Shenzhen marks their fifth contact since the beginning of this year. "Typically, the leaders begin the year with a bilateral videoconference or a phone call. This was followed by an official visit to Beijing on May 20, where a meeting was held. They also met during the SCO summit in Bishkek, and held talks during the BRICS summit in New Delhi as well," he recounted.

articles.title: Crimean Bridge attack geared to disrupt peace talks — Russian lawmaker
articles.summary: "The Ukrainian aggressor’s attacks can be interpreted as yet again spitting on the large-scale peacemaking efforts by the American side, which is trying to stop bloodshed," Mikhail Sheremet stated
articles.body: SIMFEROPOL, November 16. /TASS/. By striking the Crimean Bridge, Ukraine is seeking to derail peace talks spearheaded by the United States, a Russian lawmaker told TASS. Crimea’s head Sergey Aksyonov said earlier that Ukrainian troops had struck the Crimean Bridge, temporarily halting motor traffic. "The Ukrainian aggressor’s aggressive attacks can be interpreted as yet again spitting on the large-scale peacemaking efforts by the American side, which is trying to stop bloodshed, and the Kiev junta’s open refusal from peaceful dialogue," said Mikhail Sheremet, a member of the Russian State Duma, or lower house of parliament, from Crimea. "This lunatic Zelensky wants to continue the war while staying in his comfortable hideout abroad, as the infrastructure of his dying country is being destroyed everywhere," he added. Another State Duma member from Crimea, Leonid Ivlev, also told TASS that he thinks that Zelensky doesn’t want to end the conflict and uses any steps toward peace agreements only as an opportunity to stockpile weapons and deliver more strikes on Russia. The current Kiev regime, acting on the instructions of its Western European sponsors, is ready to commit ever greater atrocities, the lawmaker stated. "And the Crimean Bridge stood, stands, and will continue to stand, despite the Ukrainian army’s attempts to strike it and the blather of talkative bloggers who, with a cynical eye, are calculating mythical damage percentages," he added.

articles.title: Russia, UAE hold talks on cooperation in military-technical, space, banking sectors
articles.summary: A Memorandum of Understanding between the office of Russia’s Security Council and the Supreme Council for National Security of the UAE will serve to deepen cooperation
articles.body: ABU DHABI /UAE/, November 16. /TASS/. Representatives from Russia and the UAE held separate talks on cooperation in the military-technical, space, and banking sectors, Russian Security Council Secretary Sergey Shoigu said at a meeting with Secretary-General of the UAE’s Supreme Council for National Security Ali Al Shamsi. "The delegation includes high-ranking representatives from ministries and agencies responsible for cooperation with the UAE. They held separate talks with their Emirati counterparts in the following areas: military-technical cooperation, interaction in the areas of justice and law enforcement, interbank cooperation, space exploration, and the peaceful use of atomic energy," Shoigu said. A Memorandum of Understanding between the office of Russia’s Security Council and the Supreme Council for National Security of the UAE will serve to deepen cooperation, he added. The parties have signed the relevant document.

articles.title: West can't take down Russia's hypersonic missiles as claimed — expert
articles.summary: According to Alexander Stepanov, Ukraine, which is entirely dependent on foreign military technology, is currently incapable of independently producing electronic warfare systems designed to intercept ballistic weapons
articles.body: MOSCOW, November 16. /TASS/. Claims that Russia’s Oreshnik hypersonic missiles can be intercepted using electronic warfare (EW) systems are a myth that the Western military-industrial complex is trying to pass off as reality in order to save face after the total failure of missile defense systems in the Middle East, Alexander Stepanov, a military expert at the Institute of Law and National Security at the Russian Presidential Academy of National Economy and Public Administration (RANEPA)," told TASS, commenting on a New York Times article about the Lima Quant system. "Intercepting hypersonic weapons is a cherished myth of the Western military-industrial complex. They are promoting this narrative through their Ukrainian proxies, from whose positions they are, of course, testing various systems--but so far, as we can see, with little success," the expert said. According to him, Ukraine, which is entirely dependent on foreign military technology, is currently incapable of independently producing electronic warfare systems designed to intercept ballistic weapons. "If we’re to say that they are de facto incapable of countering the Kinzhal and Tsirkon missiles, then there’s no point in even discussing the Oreshnik, which surpasses them in every respect, including speed," Stepanov noted. The expert explained why it's so hard to take down a hypersonic missile. "This is due to the formation of a plasma cloud through which the warhead travels during the terminal phase, which effectively blocks any potential effect of electronic countermeasures," he said. Furthermore, the Oreshnik flies according to a flight plan with target designation that does not require corrections during the terminal phase, therefore, any interference with its navigation equipment would also be ineffective. "These claims are unfounded, technologically unjustified, and physically and materially unachievable at the current stage of development of Western defense industry technology," Stepanov emphasized. He added that the Kiev-25 production facility, where the Lima Quant device was stored, was recently shut down. "It is quite possible that tests of relevant Western solutions were conducted from a position controlled by the Kiev regime--nothing more. And, as we understand it, they were unable to prove their effectiveness in this theater of operations," the expert concluded. Earlier, a Ukrainian Night Watch territorial defense unit commander, with the call sign Alchemist, stated in an interview with The New York Times that the Lima Quant electronic warfare system diverted two Russian Oreshnik intermediate-range ballistic missiles from their targets during an attack on the Kiev Region on May 24, 2026. According to Alchemist, one missile struck garages in the Kiev Region, while the second disintegrated in flight, with its debris falling on territory under Russian control. Russian President Vladimir Putin, commenting on the situation, said that the Russian Armed Forces had struck targets where it was convenient to see the results. Russia struck a "shed" in Ukraine with an Oreshnik missile to observe how "the independently targetable warheads spread," the president said.
